headline: GPT-6 Astra writes an unchecked Deligne bound from Alpöge's RH footnote; Tesla starts FSD v15

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's quarter past one UTC on Sunday, November twenty-second. This is ARA AI News. Six hours after Lean and Mathlib certified Alpöge's Riemann Hypothesis library, an AI model has already written a second proof from a footnote, and nobody has checked that one.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Andrew Curran highlighted a Hexagon preprint tonight whose abstract says GPT six Astra, running in Chat GPT Pro, produced a short proof of Deligne's bound on Frobenius eigenvalues from a footnote in Levent Alpöge's November twentieth note.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Hexagon's own record tags the text as primarily AI-generated and says human understanding covers no parts. The provenance is unusually explicit: Claude Opus five point five wrote a research prompt on November twentieth, GPT six Astra produced the proof on November twenty-first, then Opus and Fable five point two wrote the text.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The authors say this is not a new theorem. Granted étale cohomology formalism and a weak Lefschetz theorem, they claim the argument takes less than six pages, and that its only estimate is Cauchy-Schwarz on a finite-field character sum.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: And they say no human has checked it, even though Opus and Fable checked it, which is the opposite of a refereed paper. The Hexagon deposit and GitHub check logs exist, but a named algebraic geometer has not signed off.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The bigger claim is unchanged: Lean FRO and Mathlib certified both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis in Alpöge's seventeen-million-line Lean library, depending only on Mathlib. They say Buzzard's four Xena tests pass and Andrew Sutherland's MIT checker is live, but Clay has not awarded a prize and there is still no human-readable paper.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: What to watch is a Clay Institute verdict, a public critique from Tao, Sarnak, or Soundararajan, Alpöge's promised write-up, and now whether a named algebraic geometer accepts or rejects this Hexagon note, or whether anyone Lean-formalizes the six-page argument. Anthropic is still silent on the Claude-assisted Riemann archive.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Meanwhile Tesla started putting Full Self-Driving version fifteen on cars this evening.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Tesla's rollout note claims twenty-five times better handling of safety-critical cases, a live Reality View of what the stack plans to do, better detection of signs, animals, debris, potholes, and standing water, and a Bike Rack Mode. Later version fifteen builds are meant to expand end-to-end navigation from fleet preferences to the whole route.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Elon Musk said Reality View is real-time AI video generation, not a game engine, running on half of one AI four TRIP accelerator. Tesla S I's notes add an upgraded vision encoder shared across FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, trained on millions of internet videos, and say Reality View replaces explicit model signals with a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Owner download screenshots match the posts, so the rollout and Reality View are confirmed across Tesla, Tesla S I, and owner screens. The twenty-five times figure is Tesla's own critical-intervention metric, not an independent crash study.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Watch the December holiday wider release Tesla accounts are pointing to, or a miles-and-interventions table that is not a Tesla screenshot.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: We are taking the AI-era security thread off the live board. NVIDIA's open-source agent-safety video never received a transcript, and the Mozilla Pown two Own and GPT six Cyber patch figures have not moved since mid-November.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That's a quiet close, not a verdict that the risk went away. If Daybreak or Defense Factory actually ships, that storyline comes back.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
